detail.barograph.desc: INSERT: a recording BAROGRAPH (Richard Freres style): mahogany case under a glass cover, the aneroid capsule stack, the brass linkage and the long pen arm inking a line on a paper chart (blue grid, weekdays) wrapped round a clockwork drum; at t_spike the pen jumps: the PRESSURE SPIKE of a far explosion arriving (Krakatoa 1883 was recorded on barographs worldwide, the wave passing 7 times; Tsar Bomba's went round the Earth 3 times) and falls back with a long tail; `passes` [t, ...] = later, smaller spikes (the wave coming round again). Film with an insert camera 0.25-0.6 m, limits macro

examples.note: the pen draws the spike

ship.cargo.desc: a CARGO STEAMER on the water: era 1917 (SS Mont-Blanc, Halifax: 97 m, black hull, one tall black funnel, two masts with derricks, drums of benzol stacked on the foredeck), 1947 (a Liberty ship like the Grandcamp at Texas City: 135 m, grey, midships house, three masts) or modern; `name` on the bows; fire 0..1.5 = burning on the foredeck (flames, a column of black smoke, the glow on the water); drifts along heading at speed m/s; rides the swell. Put fx.explosion type ship at its foredeck anchor for the blast

params.name: text
params.vanish: s: gone in the flash (the fx.explosion t)
params.heading: deg

examples.note: the Mont-Blanc burning in the Narrows

landmark.harbour_1917.desc: HALIFAX HARBOUR, 6 December 1917, on its own land (use biome ocean, water level 0): the Narrows (~520 m of water) between Halifax / the Richmond district (west, -x) and Dartmouth (east); wooden Piers 6-9 with long sheds on the Halifax side, the railway along the shore with boxcars and the little Richmond station (the telegraph office: film detail.wireless inside for the telegraph key), the brick Acadia sugar refinery, ~300 wooden houses in rows climbing the hill and two white churches with steeples, a few houses in Dartmouth. snow: true = a winter shore. Anchors pier6 (where the Mont-Blanc drifted, burning: put ship.cargo era 1917 and fx.explosion preset halifax there), pier7..9, station, refinery, richmond, dartmouth, narrows

params.t_blast: s: the Mont-Blanc explodes off Pier 6: the houses are knocked flat outward as the front passes (razed within ~800 m)
params.heading: deg the Narrows run (local +Z)

examples.note: the Narrows from the water, the Mont-Blanc burning off Pier 6

town.hiroshima_1945.desc: HIROSHIMA, 6 August 1945 (handled with respect: physics and objects, no people): the Ota river delta (river branches, bridges, the T-shaped Aioi Bridge), thousands of low wooden houses with dark tiled roofs along narrow streets, the brick Industrial Promotion Hall with its green copper dome (anchor dome) and a few concrete buildings. t_blast (the 15 kt air burst over ground zero = the town centre, anchor ground_zero) knocks the wooden city flat in a wave running outward (razed within ~1.8 km), the dome is stripped to its steel ribs, the concrete shells stay; fires spread from t_fire (default t_blast + 6); after: true = the flattened burning city. Put fx.nuke preset hiroshima at the town centre; film from the air 600-2500 m up, or at street level (anchor street_1km: the corner 1 km out)

examples.note: the calm aerial, then the blast flattening the city outward

landmark.atoll.desc: a CORAL ATOLL (Bikini, Enewetak): a ring of low sandy islets with coconut palms and scrub round a turquoise lagoon, the pale reef awash between them, a concrete test-site bunker on the main island. Use biome ocean. radius m of the ring (7000; the real Bikini is ~20 x 40 km: this is compressed to read in a shot). Anchors lagoon, main_island, reef_west, reef_east, outside (the open sea south of it: put ship.fishing_boat there). Castle Bravo: fx.nuke preset castle_bravo on the reef_west anchor

params.crater: true | diameter m: the Castle Bravo crater (today) in the west reef
params.heading: deg

examples.note: the atoll from the air

ship.fishing_boat.desc: the LUCKY DRAGON No. 5 (Daigo Fukuryu Maru, 1 March 1954): a 28 m wooden Japanese tuna long-liner, white hull with a red bottom, the wheelhouse aft, two masts, a line hauler, a red flag, her name in kanji on the bows (name: text to change it); rides the swell, drifts along heading at speed; ash 0..1 = the white radioactive coral ash from Castle Bravo falling on her deck (hours after the flash, 130 km away). Crew: cast figures standing on anchors deck / wheelhouse

examples.note: the Lucky Dragon under the falling ash

fx.krakatoa.desc: KRAKATOA, 27 August 1883: a volcanic island in the sea (jungle slopes, a beach, the Rakata peak ~800 m at one end, the lower Perboewatan ridge where the vent is) blown apart by the paroxysm at `t`: a white shock dome racing out over the water, the island sinking into the blast, a column of ash climbing tens of kilometres (the Plinian column of fx.eruption: jet, convecting column, umbrella, lightning, glowing bombs), pyroclastic surges racing out across the sea as a grey wall hundreds of metres high, and the tsunami ring spreading from the island. Before t an ash plume already streams from the summit. Use biome ocean (water level 0); the real hour is time-compressed. For the coast being hit use fx.tsunami at the shore; for the ship use ship.cargo era 1917 (the Norham Castle)

params.plume: m the eruption plume already standing before t (16000)
params.before: s the eruption has been going (300)
params.heading: deg of the island long axis

examples.note: the island from a ship 25 km away

space.supernova.desc: a SUPERNOVA in space (biome space): a red supergiant (Betelgeuse-like: a huge boiling red star with a few giant convection cells, strong limb darkening, a dusty red envelope) that collapses at t_collapse; at t_break the shock breaks out as a blue-white flash sweeping over its whole surface, the star balloons white-hot and fades, and the ejecta expand into a glowing filamentary shell (red filaments, teal knots, a blue glow: the Crab / Cassiopeia A look) round the tiny blue-white neutron star (pulsar: true = two rotating beams). phase 1 = the remnant already (no star). Camera: orbit_planet / approach on it (sized from radius)

params.grow: s the shell takes to expand (8)
params.shell: x the star radius the shell reaches (3.5)
params.jets: bool: a collapsar (the gamma-ray burst): two narrow white-violet jets from the poles at t_break

examples.note: the collapse and the shell

fx.supernova_sky.desc: a SUPERNOVA SEEN FROM A PLANET'S SURFACE at night (put it at the stage): a new "star" flaring at `t` whose brightness follows its distance `ly` in light-years (a type II peaks at absolute magnitude -17: at 50 ly it is ~25 x the full Moon and casts shadows, at 500 ly about a quarter Moon, at 5,000 ly a very bright star): a dazzling blue-white point, a halo, diffraction spikes, the sky round it paling, a hard light and shadows when it is bright; moon: true puts the full Moon in the sky for comparison. Use look.time night

examples.note: at 50 light-years: brighter than the Moon

space.kill_radius.desc: a SPACE DIAGRAM of a supernova's danger zone (biome space): the supernova as a blinding point, a translucent red gridded sphere of radius `ly` light-years (~50 ly: close enough to strip the ozone layer), neighbouring stars as points, and the Sun marked (a yellow point in a ring) at `sun_ly` light-years; scaled to fit (info reports metres per light-year). Put label.almanac texts on anchors sun / edge

params.sun_ly: the Sun's distance in ly (150; Betelgeuse 548)

examples.note: the kill sphere and the Sun outside it

fx.global_wave.desc: THE PRESSURE WAVE GOING ROUND THE EARTH (biome space, planets scale: Earth radius 600): the Earth from space with a pale ring racing out from the explosion site (site_lat / site_lon; default Krakatoa), shrinking to the antipode, coming back, `passes` times (Krakatoa 1883: 7 passes recorded by barographs; Tsar Bomba 1961: 3). Real circuit ~36 hours, here `period` s. The Earth faces the site (lon/lat default)

params.period: s for a full circuit there and back (8)

examples.note: Krakatoa's wave circling the globe

label.log_scale.desc: A LOG-SCALE RULER on the lens (the video's yield scale, the SAFE DISTANCE ruler in light-years, the sound-level bar): `orient` horizontal|vertical, `min`..`max` with `unit` (t = TNT yields shown as g/kg/t/kt/Mt; ly; dB; km), decade ticks, `zones` [{from, to, color, label, t_in}] (the red 50 ly danger band), `markers` [{v, label, color, t_in}] (Halifax 2.9 kt, Hiroshima 15 kt, Betelgeuse 548 ly...), a `pointer` {from, to, t, dur, label} sliding along, `zoom` {max, t, dur} (the scale extending: "the top jumping far above Halifax", "past 50 ly toward galactic scale"), `title`, `position` center|top|bottom|left|right

examples.note: the SAFE DISTANCE ruler: Earth at 1 ly, the red 50 ly band, Betelgeuse far beyond

label.verdict_board.desc: THE VERDICT BOARD (the video's scoreboard, full frame on the lens over a dark plate): five rows NOWHERE ON EARTH (black), LESS THAN A BLINK (red), SECONDS (orange), IT DEPENDS (amber), A LIFETIME (green); the cards already `placed` sit in their rows, the tray at the bottom holds the rest of the thirteen (firecracker, dynamite, grenade, moab, beirut, halifax, hiroshima, castle_bravo, tsar_bomba, krakatoa, supernova, grb, black_holes); `move` {card, row, t, dur} = a mouse cursor drags that card from the tray into its row with its personality as it lands: firecracker sparks, dynamite fuse fizzing, moab heavy thud, beirut a crack across it, halifax a tapping light, hiroshima quiet, castle_bravo white flakes, tsar_bomba oversized white, krakatoa a ring across the board, supernova / grb glow, black_holes the board ripples. slide_in: true = the board slides in at t_in

examples.note: after entry 1: the firecracker card dragged into A LIFETIME

map.blast_ring.desc: THE 1 KM RING (the video's map device): a top-down map disc on the ground (style field | village | city (streets + rivers) | harbour (quays and water) | island | atoll | ocean | quarry | arctic | desert | mountains; a stylised paper map, mustard rim) with the mustard blast crosshair in the middle, the dashed ring at ring_km labelled "1 km · 0.6 mi", the tiny Witness figure standing on the ring, danger `zones` (translucent discs or rings with their sourced labels, e.g. grenade 5 m / 15 m / 230 m, Hiroshima 2 km fire), an optional fireball outline (fireball_km: Bravo 7 km swallows the ring), map `markers` (a window, a village, a boat) and the moment: at t_flash the crosshair flashes and a white pulse races to the Witness instantly, heat: true = a heat shimmer rolling out with the light, the shock ring crawls out and reaches the Witness at t_arrive with grit swept after it; shrink: {t, dur, to_km} shrinks the ring (and the Witness) to a point labelled "0 m". Film it top-down: camera keys looking straight down from ~1.4 x size

params.size: m disc radius in the scene (40)
params.range_km: km at the disc edge (1.5 x ring)
params.label: text ("1 km · 0.6 mi")
params.zones: [{r_m, color: red|orange|pale|white|yellow|fire|#hex, label, ring: bool, t_in}]

examples.note: the grenade zones inside the 1 km ring, the shock ring reaching the Witness at 2.9 s

label.blast_clock.desc: THE BLAST CLOCK (the video's HUD, on the lens): a thin track along the bottom with five icons LIGHT, HEAT, BLAST, WIND, DEBRIS (greyed until their time), a playhead, and SURVIVED 00:00.0 counting in tenths of a second from the flash (t0). icons {light: 0, heat: 0.1, blast: 2.2, wind: 2.4, debris: 2.6} = the clock second each lights (leave one out: it stays grey); killed: s = the clock freezes RED there (the lethal moment: pair with a white frame); lifetime: s (scene time) = the clock fast-forwards and turns GREEN: A LIFETIME; paused: true = 00:00.0 blinking (the freeze). mode safe = SAFE DISTANCE in light-years (from -> to over dur): from the supernova on

params.icons: {light, heat, blast, wind, debris}: clock s
params.caption: safe mode caption
params.lift: 0..1 from the bottom (0.2 = above the subtitles)

examples.note: Hiroshima at 1 km: light and heat at 0, blast at 2.2, killed at 2.2 (red)

space.galaxy.desc: a SPIRAL GALAXY (the Milky Way) in space, face-on from above (`tilt` 0) or tilted: blue star-streaked spiral arms, pink star-forming knots, a haze, the golden bulge; `sun` [x, z] (fractions of the radius, default [0.52, 0.12]: 26,000 ly out) marked by a small ring; `burst` [x, z] + `t_burst` = a point flaring as bright as the whole galaxy (a supernova, a gamma-ray burst), `jet` (default true) = its beam drawn to the Sun; `t_red` = the whole disc shades red (nowhere in the galaxy is safe). Camera: orbit_planet on it (dist 2.2-3) or a slow push down onto it

examples.note: a burst anywhere in the galaxy with its jet aimed at the Sun; then the whole galaxy red

space.black_holes.desc: TWO BLACK HOLES merging (GW150914: 36 + 29 solar masses) in space: two black spheres ringed by bright photon rings, the starlight bent round them, spiralling in faster and faster (the chirp) and merging at t_merge into one (a quick ringdown wobble) — silent and dark, no flash; grid: true (default) = a glowing grid of spacetime below them, dimpled by their wells and stirred into a two-armed spiral of ripples that runs out in rings after the merger. Camera: orbit_planet on it (dist 2.5-3.5) or a high 3/4 view onto the grid

examples.note: the inspiral and the ripples on the spacetime grid

fx.gw_ripple.desc: GRAVITATIONAL WAVES passing through a quiet field (put it at the stage, night): faint blue-white rings sweeping over the ground from `t` for `dur` s, and the `target` figure (cast:0 = YOU) stretching tall and squeezing thin, exaggerated (`stretch` 0..0.5)

examples.note: the waves through YOU

landmark.ligo.desc: a LIGO gravitational-wave observatory (Hanford, Washington / Livingston, Louisiana): the L of two 4 km concrete arm tunnels at right angles with service roads, the white corner station and the end stations. Film it from the air (500-2500 m up)

examples.note: the L from the air

space.vela.desc: the VELA satellites (1960s nuclear-test watchers, the first to catch a gamma-ray burst in 1967): many-faced polyhedra covered in dark blue solar cells with silver edges, antennas on six sides, an X-ray detector; `count` 2 (the pair), slowly tumbling. Put space.earth far behind

examples.note: the pair in high orbit

detail.phone.desc: INSERT: a SMARTPHONE FILMING, held in a white mannequin hand in portrait (light-blue sleeve): its screen shows the LIVE view out of its back camera (the scene itself, rendered from the phone: the smoke over the port, the fireball), the camera app's red REC dot and running timer from t_rec, the shutter button; t_flash = the screen blows out orange-white. Aim it with heading (compass deg the back camera looks) + tilt, or look_at [x, z] + look_h. Put it where the Witness's hand is (1.4-1.6 m up, 0.3-0.5 m in front of the face, at a window) and film over the shoulder from 0.3-0.6 m (limits macro, fov 30-45); several at windows = the neighbours filming

examples.note: over the shoulder: the phone filming the smoke 1 km away, then the flash on its screen

landmark.balconies.desc: THE BUILDING ACROSS THE STREET (the hook, beats 007-008): a plaster apartment block with balconies on every floor (thin steel rails, dark balcony doors, a few striped awnings) and on them faceless white mannequin NEIGHBOURS in coloured shirts, most holding a phone up at eye height (screens glowing), all turned towards `look_at` [x, z] (the port). The façade faces `heading`. Film it from the Witness's window or the street, 15-40 m away

params.look_at: [x, z] world: where they all look (the port)
params.heading: deg the façade faces

examples.note: the neighbours on their balconies, all turned to the port (behind the camera)

game.npc.desc: QUEST: one chibi person (def {kit, chibi:{outfit, top, wear, crest, held, held_l, back, cape, hair, hair_color, skin, beard, expression}}); actions like the cast

game.formation.desc: QUEST: a squad / century / cohort of chibi soldiers or workers in formation (instanced, arms and legs animated, marching in step)

params.def: {kit, chibi:{...}} the look of every member
params.gap: [row, col] empty slot (the hero stands there)

game.army.desc: QUEST: a whole army / legion of thousands of chibi soldiers in blocks (count up to 6000; blocks: [[rows, cols], ...] laid side by side)

params.def: {kit, chibi:{...}} the look of every member
params.gap: [row, col] empty slot (the hero stands there)

game.crowd.desc: QUEST: a civilian crowd of mixed chibi people (kits: [...] or era), scattered, idle / talking / cheering

params.def: {kit, chibi:{...}} the look of every member
params.gap: [row, col] empty slot (the hero stands there)

biome.game_meadow.desc: QUEST toy world: low-poly bright landscape, a flat stage in the middle, faceted hills, instanced cypress / umbrella pine / round trees, flowers, puffy cartoon clouds (biome game_meadow|game_autumn|game_desert|game_snow|game_beach|game_volcano|game_moon; trees 0..2, clouds 0..2, clear m, features road/river/clearing/hill, water sea|lake)

biome.game_autumn.desc: QUEST toy world: autumn (low-poly, the game look's biome; same params as biome.game_meadow)

biome.game_desert.desc: QUEST toy world: desert (low-poly, the game look's biome; same params as biome.game_meadow)

biome.game_snow.desc: QUEST toy world: snow (low-poly, the game look's biome; same params as biome.game_meadow)

biome.game_beach.desc: QUEST toy world: beach (low-poly, the game look's biome; same params as biome.game_meadow)

biome.game_volcano.desc: QUEST toy world: volcano (low-poly, the game look's biome; same params as biome.game_meadow)

biome.game_moon.desc: QUEST toy world: moon (low-poly, the game look's biome; same params as biome.game_meadow)

game.level_map.desc: QUEST: the level map seen from above: numbered pads joined by white paths winding to the final building; the current level glows, passed pads turn gold, a crossed-out pad shows a red line

game.pad.desc: QUEST: one level pad: a white disc with a gold rim, glowing when active; the hero stands on it

game.chest.desc: QUEST: a treasure chest that opens at t_open and bursts gold coins (pays out)

game.coins.desc: QUEST: a pile of gold coins, or coins raining down from t (rain: true)

game.ring.desc: QUEST: a big floating golden ring with a red gem, turning and bobbing, glowing (a reward, a rank, an unlock)

game.trophy.desc: QUEST: a floating reward object turning in the air: trophy|crown|gem|key|scroll|star|medal|coin|book|potion

game.gate.desc: QUEST: the final level: a monumental golden gate between sandstone pillars; the doors swing open at t_open and warm light pours out

game.camp.desc: QUEST: a fortified camp: a square ditch and earth rampart with a palisade, gates on each side and rows of tents; builds itself over build:[t0, t1] (ditch, walls, then tents pop in)

game.road.desc: QUEST: a straight paved road with kerbs and milestone pillars (Roman road) from -> to

game.column.desc: QUEST: a white stone column (fluted, low-poly), optional broken

game.temple.desc: QUEST: a toy Greek / Roman temple: stepped base, columns, pediment (white, red roof optional)

game.wall.desc: QUEST: a stone wall segment with crenellations from -> to (city wall, fort)

game.house.desc: QUEST: a toy house (style roman|medieval|village|modern|hut|igloo|japanese), colour roof

game.castle.desc: QUEST: a toy castle: four towers, walls, a keep, flags

game.tower.desc: QUEST: a round watchtower with a cone roof

game.post.desc: QUEST: a wooden training post (palus) planted in the ground

game.standard.desc: QUEST: a standard on a pole: aquila (golden eagle), banner (colour) or flag

game.beam.desc: QUEST: a vertical column of golden light (a level-up / a quest spot), fading in at t and out at t_out

game.burst.desc: QUEST: a level-up burst at t: a ring wave on the ground, gold sparkles flying up, a flash

game.campfire.desc: QUEST: a campfire with flickering flames and glow

game.crates.desc: QUEST: a stack of crates, barrels and sacks (supplies, loot, a market)

game.ship.desc: QUEST: a toy wooden ship with a sail (galley|sailship|longship), sailing along its heading at speed

game.cart.desc: QUEST: a two-wheeled cart (hand cart or ox cart without the ox), moving along its heading at speed

game.sign.desc: QUEST: a wooden signpost with arrows (text on it)

game.tag.desc: QUEST world-space game UI over a target: a name plate, YOU ▼, a red danger ⚠ + bar, a health bar, a quest "!", a counting number, a damage number

params.offset: [dx, dy, dz] above the target top
params.at: [x, z] when not on a thing

game.select.desc: QUEST RTS selection box drawn on the ground round a group (on: groups:N) or a radius at [x, z]: green outline, corner brackets, translucent fill, drawn in at t_in

game.horse.desc: QUEST: a chibi toy horse (color brown|chestnut|bay|black|white|grey|palomino, caparison #hex for a knight's draped horse), idle or walking / trotting / galloping along its heading or a path; a rider: {def} sits on it (or give a cast member the action ride)

archive.photo.desc: ARCHIVE: one real archival print (src photo) with a white border, slight curl, matte or glossy, aged; a typed name on the bottom border and a bold epithet that decodes in (fern). Lies flat (tilt deg props it up)

params.label: typed name on the border
params.label2_t: s: when label2 decodes (default: always typed)
params.elev: m above the ground (0.76 on a desk)

archive.desk.desc: ARCHIVE: fern's dossier desk — a dark plank desk under ONE warm lamp; real prints (src) with typed labels, maps, documents, folders, telegrams, an insignia patch, overlapping at angles; items slide in from a frame edge (enter_t) and settle; clutter (pen, magnifier, ashtray + smoking cigarette, paper clips, coffee ring); dust in the lamp light. Film it top-down (pitch -75..-85 deg, fov 30-35, 0.8-1.1 m above the top, slow push) with a rack focus between item_N anchors

params.items: [{src | kind: photo|map|doc|insignia|folder|telegram, at: [x, z] desk m from its centre (+z = reader), rot deg, w m, label, label2, label2_t, enter_t, enter_from: left|right|top|bottom, enter_dist m (0.5), enter_dur s (1.1), clip: bool, text, title, stamp}]
params.lamp: true | banker (a visible green lamp) | false
params.clutter_at: {pen, magnifier, ashtray, coffee: [x, z]} (default: placed in the pile round the hero)

archive.wall.desc: ARCHIVE: an investigation wall — cork, plaster or a big map as the board, real prints and papers pinned, RED STRING drawn from pin to pin (strings_t), a warm lamp grazing it

params.items: [{src | kind, at: [x, y] board m from its centre, rot, w, label, label2}]
params.strings_t: s: first string starts drawing (each 0.5 s later)

archive.frame.desc: ARCHIVE: a framed real photo (wood, gilt or steel frame, mat, glass with a soft reflection) on a wall or standing on a desk on its strut

archive.projector.desc: ARCHIVE: a 16 mm projector in a dark room playing a real film sequence on a screen: reels turning, a visible BEAM with dust motes and the film light in it, flicker; anything standing in the beam catches the picture (silhouettes in front of the screen). Put the camera beside / behind the projector, 1-2 m off the beam

archive.screen.desc: ARCHIVE: a screen or hanging sheet playing a real film sequence (no projector), glowing on a dark room

archive.tv.desc: ARCHIVE: a period CRT television (1940s-80s) playing a real sequence: curved glass, scanlines, phosphor glow, flicker, a rolling bar

params.elev: m (0 = a console on the floor)
params.lamp: true: a dim warm room lamp to one side | false

archive.filmstrip.desc: ARCHIVE: a 35 mm film strip (sprockets, edge code) as a ribbon snaking through space, every frame a still of the sequence, scrolling; backlit

archive.float.desc: ARCHIVE: a 2.5D parallax photo — one real photo split into depth layers floating in a void or the sky, drifting; a camera move gives real parallax (push / truck 0.3-1 m across it)

params.edge: feather (default: melts into the void) | hard

archive.relief.desc: ARCHIVE: the real portrait as a relief: the photo displaced by its depth and lit by real light — a red slit gobo sliding across the face in a black void (fern red-slit beat, real likeness, no CG face)

params.slit_color: #ff7048 (x the gobo: deep-red edges, orange core)
params.fill: 0..1 dim warm fill outside the slit (0.045)
params.rim: 0..1 cool side-back rim (0 with the slit, 0.25 otherwise)

archive.paper_label.desc: ARCHIVE: a typed paper strip as an object in the world (on a desk, a wall, a box): off-white, dark typewriter text that decodes in at t_in

light.spot.desc: ONE MOTIVATED LIGHT (fern): a spotlight with a projected cookie - a vertical SLIT of light across a face in a black void, BLINDS stripes over a figure at a desk, a WINDOW cross on a wall, prison BARS, FOLIAGE dapple, a projector GATE - with an optional visible beam in smoky air (dust motes drifting in it), real shadows, keep_hue (the red slit stays red when the shot is graded blue). It follows a moving target. Put it in `objects`. Pair with stage.void for the antagonist portrait.

params.at: [x, z] where the lamp hangs (+ y), or from [az deg around the target from its front (+ = toward its right hand), el deg, dist m]
params.target: what it lights: 'ref:<castId>' | 'objects:N' | [x, y, z] | [x, z] (follows a moving target)
params.intensity: candela at exposure 1 (40; the slit 60-120, a rim 20-60)
params.cookie_opts: {w, n, duty, cols, rows, ...}; slit {w 0.042, len 0.95, band 0.22 (glow band round the hot core), band_w 1.9}
params.beam: 0..1 visible beam in the air (raymarched, smoke + dust)
params.haze: 0..1 the air density in the beam (0.55)
params.keep_hue: true: its colour survives a mono grade (the red slit in a blue world)
params.spill: 0..1 a soft wide uncookied bounce of the same colour (0.25-0.3 with a slit: the uniform around it reads as a dark maroon form, fern T07)
params.spill_drop: m the spill aims below the target (0.65: the chest, so the face outside the slit stays dark)
params.spill_angle: deg (3.2 x angle, >= 16; 9-10 keeps it off the face)
params.range: m the light dies out (0 = never; set it so a slit does not reach the figures behind)
params.sweep: {m: 0.12, t: [t0, t1]} the light slides across its target: m = the whole slide in metres AT THE TARGET (0.12 = across a face; from_m / to_m offsets); a slit is clamped to +-0.09 m

light.rig.desc: A LIGHT RIG RIDING A CAST MEMBER: coloured key / rim / fill spots that move with the figure and aim at its head (fern colour code: red = the perpetrator, blue = the heroes, amber = home). Rim light from behind separates a dark figure from a black void. Put it in `objects`.

params.subject: 'ref:<castId>' (alias on)
params.key: colour | {color, intensity, az, el, dist, angle, cookie}
params.rim: colour | {color, intensity, az (142 = behind a shoulder; mirrored for the other side), el, dist, aim: head|chest}
params.fade: [t0, dur] the whole rig fades up (assassins appearing)

light.practical.desc: A VISIBLE PRACTICAL LIGHT: a bare bulb on a cord, a desk lamp throwing a pool on the desk, or the paratroopers' JUMP LIGHT that switches red -> green at t_switch; optional flicker (a failing bulb, a candle). Put it in `objects`.

params.t_switch: s (jump: red goes out, 0.12 s later green comes on)
params.heading: deg (lamp / jump face)

stage.void.desc: FERN'S BLACK VOID STAGE: the subject alone on an empty black stage, lit only by a slit, a rim or a spot (light.spot / light.rig) - the antagonist portrait, a symbolic object, a line-up. No terrain, no sky, no ambient light. Optional floor that shows only where light falls (gloss reflects the lights), a dark floor glow that fades up under the subject, haze so the beams show, and figures that RISE out of the darkness. Put it in `objects`; add the lights; frame from 1.8-6 m.

params.glow: {color, r m, intensity, fade: [t0, dur], keys: [{t, i}], at: [x, z], backdrop: true, y} (or a LIST of them) a dark floor glow under the subject (fern: #0a1640 blue); backdrop: a soft disc standing behind the figures facing the lens (the haze dark silhouettes read against; with a floor it fades out toward the floor). keys: eased intensity multipliers - e.g. the haze at 0.25 from frame 1 (the officer's cap and shoulders read as a silhouette) rising to 1 on the beat. A small backdrop halo BETWEEN the hero and the figures behind hides them until their own light comes up
params.rise: [{ref: 'ref:<castId>', t, dur, depth m}] figures come up from below the darkness, eased (floor none only; with a floor they fade up from darkness, no lift)

fog.volume.desc: A LOCAL FOG / SMOKE VOLUME: a box, a sphere or a low ground layer of drifting smoke - lit by any light.spot beam that passes through it (a beam turns solid in it) and hiding what is behind it. For the smoke floor of a void stage, haze in a room, valley fog. Put it in `objects`.

params.shape: box|sphere|layer|plume (a rising lit smoke COLUMN from a fire / a burning ship / a chimney: h, r, spread, fire, drift = wind)
params.glow: 0..1 self-glow so it reads without a beam (0.05)
params.drift: [vx, vy, vz] m/s the smoke drifts (wind; [0.12, 0.03, 0] = a slow lateral drift: a moving layer in a still shot)
params.fire: plume: 0..1 flames + an orange glow at its base
params.lean: plume: [dx, dz] m the top is carried downwind (default from drift)

aircraft.halifax.desc: Handley Page Halifax Mk II four-engine RAF night bomber (SOE special duties, 1941-42): twin square fins, four Merlin nacelles with glowing flame-damper exhausts and spinning props, nose / mid-upper / tail turrets, matt black night finish; interior: true opens a hold with ribs, a plank floor, the floor "Joe hole" hatch, static-line cable, benches (seat_0..3 deck points), red/green jump light and moonlight up through the hatch. Anchors (target them as objects:N.<anchor>; a bare objects:N is measured from the ground under it): body, nose, cockpit, tail, wing_l (port), wing_r (starboard), engine_1..4 (port outer .. starboard outer), door, hatch_below; interior: hatch, hatch_edge (stand point at the forward rim, facing aft: hatch_sit), seat_0..3 (benches, 0/1 starboard, 2/3 port), hold, jump_light

params.heading: deg (0 = north)
params.speed: m/s (default 62; 0 = holds still: the airframe frame, give the cloud layer wind -airspeed)
params.alt: m above the ground at `at` (default 900), then flown level
params.keys: [{t, roll deg (+ = starboard wing down), pitch deg (+ nose up), yaw deg, dy m}] eased attitude offsets, e.g. [{t:0, roll:12}, {t:1.4, roll:0}]
params.interior: true: the enterable hold (ribs, floor, Joe hole, benches, jump light)
params.hatch_open: true (default) | false | t: opens at t (0.8 s)
params.jump_light: {red: t (default 0), green: t}: the jump light turns green at t
params.static_lines: 0..4 (the first N seats) | [seat indices]: static lines from the roof cable to the seats

sky.cloud_layer.desc: enterable volumetric cloud deck (moonlit / sunlit cumulus-stratocumulus) over any world: fly into it, through it and out; seen from below, inside and above with no seams; a carved tunnel corridor for an aircraft, gaps down to the ground, wind, speed streaks. Night: silver moonlit edges, blue whiteout inside

params.base: m above the ground at the stage (default 800)
params.gaps: 0..1 big holes down to the ground (default 0.3)
params.tunnel: {from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z] | via: [[x,y,z]...] | follow: "objects:N" (+ t: [t0, t1]: the stretch of its flight that is carved; the lens behind the t0 end starts inside the cloud), radius m (default 45), fog 0..1 (thin wisps left in the corridor, default 0.3)}: a corridor through the deck (world y)
params.near: m: cloud fades out this close to the lens (default 5)
params.inner: 0..0.5 patchy fog inside the deck between the billows (default 0.1; 0.25 = a long whiteout when the lens starts deep inside)
params.fill: 0.3..1 how solid a fully covered deck is (default 0.8: billows with dark gaps)
params.scatter: 0..3 multiple-scattering glow of the cloud body (default 1)
params.wind: [x, z] m/s (the cloud field moves; e.g. [0, -62] past an aircraft held still heading 180)
params.moon: {az, el}: the light direction (default: the scene key light)
params.streaks: 0..1 speed streaks round a fast lens (default 0)
params.haze: 0..1 air between the clouds and below the deck (default 0.4)
params.fog_in: true | {t0, t1 (default 0, 0.9 s), depth m (120), density (1)}: the lens starts inside a cloud bank whose front face sweeps back past it (fern C1: 0-0.5 s blue whiteout, then the aircraft emerges)
params.far: m: the deck continues analytically to here and fades into the horizon haze (default 120000)

para.jumper.desc: a paratrooper in the air: exit -> free fall -> canopy deploy (eased, no pops) -> descent swinging under an X-type canopy -> landing; any kit (para_soe default) or a cast ref
para.jumper.doc: Static-line drop of 1941: free fall is UPRIGHT, feet first, hands on the harness (not a skydiver arch). Params: at [x, z] + y (absolute m; the registry drops the y of a 3-element at) or alt (m above the ground, 250); kit para_soe | any kit, or ref (a video cast id: the identical figure in every scene); heading (aircraft heading deg: he leaves along it); exit_speed (aircraft m/s, 45: the throw-forward the air brakes in ~1 s); t_exit (s he leaves the hatch, 0.3; pre "hide" = invisible before, "hatch" = sitting in the hatch moving with the aircraft); t_deploy (s of line stretch; static line 0.6-1.2 s after the exit; default t_exit + 1.0); open (inflation s 0.6-0.9, 0.85); phases [exit, freefall, deploy, descent, landing] (the first one listed is where the scene starts: descent = already under the open canopy at t 0); fall_speed (terminal m/s, 53); descent (m/s under the canopy, 5.5); drift [vx, vz] wind m/s; sway 0..1.5 (swing under the canopy, 0.6); wobble 0..2 (free-fall wobble, 1); tumble true (whole turns before line stretch); look down|up|ahead (head under the canopy); canopy {color olive|khaki|white|sand|grey|camo|hex, diameter 8.5 flat m, lines m, translucency 0.32}; face (deg added to his yaw); hide_after (s); silhouette 0..1 (darkens his kit: 0.6-0.8 = the fern look, dark cut-outs against a night sky). positionAt(t) = the harness point (x, y, z) for cameras that fall with him; anchors body (the figure), canopy (the dome centre), rig (his chest in free fall, sliding up to the middle of the rig once the canopy opens). Camera targets: freefall_follow / chase on one jumper: objects:N (or objects:N.jumper_0); a deploy inside a follow shot: target objects:N.rig and rel back >= 16 m (the 10 m rig must fit); on a para.stick ALWAYS name the jumper (objects:N.jumper_0 / rig_0): objects:N alone frames the whole stick as one rigid box and the lead leaves the frame. Cameras: one that falls WITH him (keys whose y follows positionAt(t), or WP1 freefall_follow) 6-8 m away, looking up 15-25 deg, FOV 38-45; canopies from below: the camera keeps falling (25-40 m/s, slowing) while they decelerate, so the canopies rise through the frame 20-35 m away; descent: match `descent` m/s, 18-30 m from the canopy so the whole rig (canopy + lines + man, ~10 m) fits. Never closer than 3 m to the figure.

para.stick.desc: a stick of N paratroopers leaving one aircraft `spacing` s apart (each with its own canopy); anchors jumper_N / canopy_N
para.stick.doc: Camera: on a stick target ONE jumper: objects:N.jumper_0 (the lead; jumper_1 ...), objects:N.rig_0 for a deploy inside a follow shot; objects:N alone = the whole stick as one rigid box (WP1 freefall_follow then frames the box and the lead leaves the frame). n jumpers (default the length of jumpers, else 2); spacing s between exits (0.9; the aircraft moves exit_speed x spacing between them); jumpers [{ref | kit, colors, t_exit, t_deploy, descent, at, y, ...}] per-jumper overrides; vary 0..1 per-jumper variation of descent, sway and yaw (0.5). Every para.jumper key applies to all of them: Params: at [x, z] + y (absolute m; the registry drops the y of a 3-element at) or alt (m above the ground, 250); kit para_soe | any kit, or ref (a video cast id: the identical figure in every scene); heading (aircraft heading deg: he leaves along it); exit_speed (aircraft m/s, 45: the throw-forward the air brakes in ~1 s); t_exit (s he leaves the hatch, 0.3; pre "hide" = invisible before, "hatch" = sitting in the hatch moving with the aircraft); t_deploy (s of line stretch; static line 0.6-1.2 s after the exit; default t_exit + 1.0); open (inflation s 0.6-0.9, 0.85); phases [exit, freefall, deploy, descent, landing] (the first one listed is where the scene starts: descent = already under the open canopy at t 0); fall_speed (terminal m/s, 53); descent (m/s under the canopy, 5.5); drift [vx, vz] wind m/s; sway 0..1.5 (swing under the canopy, 0.6); wobble 0..2 (free-fall wobble, 1); tumble true (whole turns before line stretch); look down|up|ahead (head under the canopy); canopy {color olive|khaki|white|sand|grey|camo|hex, diameter 8.5 flat m, lines m, translucency 0.32}; face (deg added to his yaw); hide_after (s); silhouette 0..1 (darkens his kit: 0.6-0.8 = the fern look, dark cut-outs against a night sky). positionAt(t) = the harness point (x, y, z) for cameras that fall with him; anchors body (the figure), canopy (the dome centre), rig (his chest in free fall, sliding up to the middle of the rig once the canopy opens). Camera targets: freefall_follow / chase on one jumper: objects:N (or objects:N.jumper_0); a deploy inside a follow shot: target objects:N.rig and rel back >= 16 m (the 10 m rig must fit); on a para.stick ALWAYS name the jumper (objects:N.jumper_0 / rig_0): objects:N alone frames the whole stick as one rigid box and the lead leaves the frame.

para.canopy.desc: an X-type round canopy (28 gores, vent, scalloped skirt, lines, risers): open | streamer | collapsed | deploy; load none | container
para.canopy.doc: at [x, z] + alt (m above the ground, 30) or y (absolute); state open | streamer | collapsed | deploy (opens at t_deploy, eased); descent m/s (0 = hanging still); drift [vx, vz]; load container (a supply container under it); color olive | white | khaki | sand | grey | camo | hex; diameter flat m (8.5). collapsed = LYING ON THE GROUND (the buried-parachute beat): the riser links at `at`, the crumpled cloth 5-10 m downwind (drift, else heading) on the terrain under every vertex, the lines over the snow to the links, the wind lifting it slowly; frame it from 6-12 m at eye level or from above. Camera templates frame the canopy itself (subjectAt: the rig middle in the air, the sheet on the ground).

figure.bust.desc: a faceless portrait bust cut from a dressed figure (default kit ss_officer): plaster | bronze | marble | painted | dark, on a plinth or floating; optional slit / rim light and a black void
figure.bust.doc: Params: kit (ss_officer) or ref (a video cast id) + colors / headwear; material plaster | bronze | marble | painted | dark; mount plinth (plinth_h m, 1.0) | floating (float_h m = the cut height, 1.05); cut chest | waist | m (1.1); turn deg (head), chin deg (4); light {slit: colour, slit_w m (full band width 0.055), slit_x m across the face (0.034: over one eye), slit_from deg (15), slit_i (1.0), rim: colour, rim_i (3), rim_h m above the cut (0.25 shoulders; 0.75 = cap + head outline), key: colour, key_i, key_sweep deg (the key travels round the bust over the shot), spill (0.3: the soft red of the slit on the uniform and the face)}; dust 0..1 (motes drifting in the light); headwear none (bare-headed, like the fern bust); skin hex (head + hands under painted; grey by default with a slit); void true (black void + pitch dark); flank {n 2, kit civil_coat_1940s | refs [...], action aim_pistol_2h, t_in s, fade s (0.8), rim colour (#3a62ff), rim_i (30), dist m behind (2.4), spread m (1.45), turn deg inward (22), floor colour (#0a1640) | false}: the assassins who fade up behind him in blue rims. The antagonist portrait of the fern void beat: eye-level camera 1.6-3 m away, slow push 0.5 %/s, a red slit across the face (light.slit or WP3 light.spot cookie slit), blue-rim figures behind. It reads by its silhouette: keep the cap and the collar in a rim light. Never a lit close-up under 1 m. Under a mono grade (WP3 void_blue / nocturne / archive_bw) the slit registers itself as a keep_hue light and stays red; add look.keep_hue '#ff2a14' for any other red in the frame.

town.bohemian_village.desc: Czech/Bohemian village c.1900-1945 round its long village green (naves): one-storey gable-fronted farmhouses with yard walls and arched gates, barns behind, a baroque church on the green (white plaster, ochre pilasters, west tower with clock, belfry and a dark onion helmet + lantern), frozen pond, bare lindens, snowy rutted roads; blackout = only `lit` windows glow; chimney smoke drifts; a lamp glows in the belfry at night. The occupied homeland at night in the snow.

params.heading: deg compass of the green's long axis (default 90)
params.tower_glow: 0..1 lamp in the belfry at night (default 0.6)

landmark.prague_castle.desc: Prague Castle (Hradcany) on its ridge as seen across the Vltava: the long pale south wing with rows of windows, St Vitus Cathedral rising behind it (the great south tower with its copper helmet and lantern ~99 m, the two needle west spires ~82 m, copper nave roof, flying buttresses), the Old Royal Palace roof, St George's twin towers, the Black Tower, palaces of Hradcany square, gardens and ramparts down the slope, the Lesser Town roofs and the St Nicholas dome below. Windows lit at dusk/night. Built at true scale (~680 m wide): film it from 400-1200 m.

params.at: [x, z] centre of the palace front (top of the ridge)
params.heading: deg compass the front faces (toward the river / the camera; default 180)
params.lit: 0..1 share of windows lit at night (default 0.18; 1942 blackout: 0.05)

town.prague_1942.desc: a Prague street c.1900-1945: a canyon of 4-6 storey baroque / neo-renaissance / art-nouveau houses (stucco facades in ochre, cream, grey, salmon; recessed windows with surrounds, pediments, pilasters, cornices with modillions, mansards with dormers, shop fronts with sign boards, portals, some balconies), granite-sett carriageway, slab pavements on granite kerbs, double tram track with overhead contact wires on span wires, cast-iron gas lamps (lit at dusk: light pools + a few real lights), cross streets; bend for a curve (preset holesovice = the Heydrich attack curve: a sharp bend with an iron railing on stone posts and trees on the inside). Cars and trams follow it with road: <id>.

params.heading: deg compass the street runs (default 90)
params.lamp_lights: 0..6 real lights at the lamps nearest light_at (default 3)
params.close: true|false (default true: a cross street + a row of houses closes both ends, no void down the street)

vehicle.mercedes_320.desc: Mercedes-Benz 320 open staff car (W142 Cabriolet B, Heydrich's car): long bonnet with louvres, upright chrome radiator with the star, separate sweeping front fenders running into running boards, bowl headlamps with blackout slits, chrome bumpers, raked windscreen, folded top (or up), red leather seats, whitewall tyres with chrome hubcaps, spare on the tail, two fender flags that flutter with speed; seated faceless riders (default 2: driver + officer in peaked caps). Drives a path or a Prague street lane (road: <town id>).

params.heading: deg compass (0 = north)
params.path: [[x, z], ...] waypoints (smoothed to the turning radius)
params.road: '<id>' of a town.prague_1942: drive its lane instead of a path (the car stays ON the street)
params.lane: right (default: right-hand traffic, 1939+) | left | track | metres from the centre
params.from: m along the street where it starts
params.to: m along the street where it ends
params.start: s: from rest at this time (eased)
params.stop: true: eases to rest at the path end
params.turn_radius: m

vehicle.tram_prague.desc: 1930s Prague tram (two-axle motor car): dark red lower panels, cream window band and letterboard, curved platform dashes, clerestory roof, route box, trolley pole on the 5.65 m contact wire, saloon lit warm at dusk, occasional blue sparks at the trolley wheel. Runs a path or a Prague street track (road: <town id>, track 0|1).

params.heading: deg compass (0 = north)
params.path: [[x, z], ...] waypoints (smoothed to the turning radius)
params.road: '<id>' of a town.prague_1942: drive its lane instead of a path (the car stays ON the street)
params.lane: right (default: right-hand traffic, 1939+) | left | track | metres from the centre
params.from: m along the street where it starts
params.to: m along the street where it ends
params.start: s: from rest at this time (eased)
params.stop: true: eases to rest at the path end
params.turn_radius: m

core.plain.desc: Fallback world: open plain with gentle relief and far hills (features: road, ridge)

core.crowd.desc: Group of faceless mannequins in a formation

camera.target: stage | ref:<castId> | groups:N | objects:N | structures:N | labels:N | [x, z]
camera.keys: move keys: [{t, pos: [x,y,z] | at: [x,z] + alt, look: [x,y,z] | look_at: [x,z] + look_h, fov}] (fov per key = an eased lens track), limits: eye (1.3 m) | macro (0.15 m)
camera.lens: [{t, fov}] a lens track on any move (monotone, eased)
camera.dolly_zoom: {t: [t0, t1], fov: end_deg, target}: vertigo shot, the target keeps its size while the lens changes (smaller fov = camera backs away)
camera.focus: [{t, target: 'ref:you' | 'objects:0' | 'objects:0.<anchor>' | [x,y,z] | 'infinity', fstop: 1.4..16, pull: s}] rack focus between real positions (replaces dof)
camera.shake: [{t, amp: deg 0.2..2.5, dur: s <= 2.5, freq: Hz 1.5..14, attack: s}] designed impact shake: rare (one impact per shot), short, eased
camera.handheld: 0..1 slow operator drift for eye-level documentary shots (never shaky)
camera.strict: true: the path is final (no lift, relax or flyover fallback); a failing path is reported, not rendered
camera.fpv_dive: move fpv_dive (E2 v2): one smooth spline from high above (altitude [start, end], default [~1.1 x length, 160..320], [.., pull-up]) diving at the target, skimming past it at `height` m (default: the `pass` anchor's height, else 0.8 x its top) `skim` m clear of its `side` (left = its port), then pulling up (end rise) or away (end away); pass: '<ref>.<anchor>' e.g. 'titanic.funnel_2'; approach: ahead (default for a moving subject: a head-on pass) | astern; fov default 62. The speed is fitted to dur within the safety rule (the start altitude and the skim shrink for a short dur); looks along the flight turned toward the hull, banks <= 6.5 deg. 7-10 s works best
camera.tracking_low: move tracking_low (E2 v2): rides beside a MOVING target at its exact velocity, `height` m over the water / ground (default 3), `offset` m out from its `side` (left = port; default 0.1 x length + 5), at `lead` (fraction of the length ahead of the centre, -0.5..0.5, default 0.12) drifting to `lead_end`, looking at `look_lead` along the hull (default 0.45 = the bow and its bow wave) at `look_h` m; fov default 38. Speed rules are measured relative to the subject (the drift along the hull is kept legal)
camera.approach: move approach (E4 v2, space): target a space.* body; from a far dot to it filling the frame, an exponential (log-distance) zoom. from: 30 (radii from the centre; 60+ = a real dot, the frame check then calls the first frames black), to: 1.45 (3.2 with rings), az/el: the side it comes from (deg; default 0 / 8 = from +Z), arc: 14 (deg of drift round it), look_off: 0 (radii to aim above the centre at the end), fov 34. 5-10 s
camera.orbit_planet: move orbit_planet (E4 v2, space): target a space.* body; a sweeping orbit round it: dist 2.3 (radii; 3.4 with rings), arc 40 (deg), el / el_end (deg), az (start), side left|right, look_off, fov 40. sunrise: true = a low orbit (dist 1.1) over the limb looking at the horizon ahead; the Sun rises over it at rise_at (0.55 of the shot), horizon 0.62 (where the horizon sits, 0 top .. 1 bottom), yaw 8 (deg the Sun sits off centre); it sets the scene's sun unless look.sun / world.sun is given. 6-12 s
camera.map_dive: move map_dive with a space.* target (E4 v2): from `from` 2.4 radii above the surface point facing the camera (the body's lon/lat) down to `to` 0.025 radii, pitching from straight down to the horizon (end: 'down' stays down); point: [x, y, z] world direction from the centre to dive at. Cut to that world's surface biome after it. 5-8 s. Other targets: crane_down as before
camera.fall_through: move fall_through (E4 v2): a vertical descent through cloud decks (biome.jupiter_clouds ...) or an atmosphere: from / to (world y; defaults: 700 -> -5200 in a cloud world, 900 m -> 6 m over real ground), curve terminal (fast, then slowing: the default in cloud worlds) | accelerate | linear | log (altitude-proportional: the default over ground, keeps the speed rule), spin 40 (deg of yaw over the shot), yaw (start heading), pitch -62 (deg; -86 straight down, 0 the horizon) -> pitch_end, drift [dx, dz] m, at [x, z], fov 60. 6-12 s
camera.profile: camera.profile 'fpv' (v3): FPV limits (roll <= 30 deg, roll rate 75 deg/s, turn 140 deg/s, eased turns, jerk-free C2 paths, speed <= 1.6 x clearance below 60 m, clearance 1 m / 2.5 m above 15 m/s, figures 0.8 m, never shortened, never lifted) and the bank from lateral acceleration (bank_max 18, max 30). Implied by every FPV move below. On keys: the key POSITIONS are kept and re-timed on an even arc-length speed under the cap (the new key times are reported); a line too long for its time ends before its last keys (warning with the duration it needs) unless reshape: true lifts its low stretches
camera.freefall_follow: move freefall_follow (v3 FPV): falls WITH a falling target (para.jumper / space.astronaut float with drift [0,-48,0] / prop.bomb / any flying item) at its speed: rel [side, up, back] m in its frame (default [3, 1.5, 7]; up < 0 = below looking up at it against the sky), orbit deg over the shot (<= 40), drift_in 0..1 (an even approach; 1 + transition.out {kind:'occlude', by: <target>, frames: 10} = it passes the lens in the last frames: the hidden cut; with fewer frames the lens starts farther away), wobble 0..1 (0.35), aim [x, y], look_up deg, fov 42. Near the ground the camera FLARES (stops >= 30 m up while the subject drops away below); the notes give the impact time. 3-5 s
camera.chase: move chase (v3 FPV): rides a moving target's own PAST TRACK (where it was `back` m ago: the same road, the same line, the same corners a beat later): offset [side, up, back] m where back is the TRUE distance (default: fitted so it spans fill 0.5 of the frame width: bomber ~30-40 m, fighter 10-16 m, car 6-8 m), weave m, lead m, banks with its turns (bank_max 18..30, track_sigma 0.5 s, roll rate soft-capped at 60 deg/s), fov 50. A car at speed keeps the lens >= 2.9 m over the road. Aircraft, cars, trains, horses. 3-8 s
camera.proximity_pass: move proximity_pass (v3 FPV): skims past a target's real mesh boxes at clearance m (2.5; 1.2-4 looks fast and safe), speed m/s (18; 8 relative when it moves), along length|span, side left|right|over|under, dir forward|back (a moving target overtakes the lens by default: the camera starts beside its middle, the tail passes ~1 s in, it pulls away ahead), pass_at (0.8 for a still target or dir forward: it is ahead, in frame, most of the shot), height m above its base (auto: under / over a wing beside the fuselage; a tower or spire: beside it at 40-70 % of its height), bulge m, glance 0..1, keep_dev deg (75: the lens turns toward it to keep it in frame), fov 70. Wings, hulls, towers, a church spire. 2.5-4 s
camera.orbit_reveal: move orbit_reveal (v3 FPV): spiral orbit round the target: r0 -> r1 m (default 2.2 x size + 2 -> 0.62 x r0), deg of arc (120, <= 300; side left = the other way), rise m (0.3 x r0), h0 m above its centre, az (start compass deg; default: chosen so the arc stays clear and ends facing the structure behind the target), look_h, aim [x, y], fov 45. Indoors (an interior.* room) the radius dips round columns and walls and relax tightens; lean <= 3 deg; raised if too fast for its height. A bust in a void, canopies, a landmark, a figure in a hall. 4-8 s
camera.fpv_line: move fpv_line (v3 FPV): the director's flown line through via waypoints (C2): [x, y, z] | [x, z] (+alt m, default 3) | '<ref>' (its centre when the camera passes) | {target, offset: [right, up, forward]}; frame: '<ref>' = the line rides that moving item and via are [right, up, forward] in its frame or its anchor names ('ramp', 'tail', 'nose'); speed m/s (cruise; default fits the shot, even speed <= 1.45 x mean, <= 1.6 x clearance over roofs and treetops), reshape (default: a line too long for its time at its heights gets its low stretches lifted so every waypoint is reached; false = it ends early with a warning), ease_in 0.7, look_ahead s (0.35), look_at '<ref>' + look_w 0..1 (0.6), tilt deg (-4), fov 72. Waypoints >= 8 m from walls and treetops. 3-8 s
camera.cloud_tunnel: move cloud_tunnel (v3 FPV): fern's cold-open reveal on an aircraft target: starts length m behind it (1.4 L, >= 35) and below (below m), swings in from the side (banks ~10-15 deg, levels the horizon over the last 30 %), emerges under the tail at emerge_t s (0.42 x dur) and closes on it; with transition.out {kind:'occlude', by: <target>} it flies into the belly in the last frames (the last frame is skin on every frustum ray: the hidden cut). documentary.desc: today's look: stylized realism, faceless white mannequins, film light (no preset)

san_andreas.desc: PS2-era San Andreas: a soft 448-line frame upscaled bilinear, the orange timecyc colour filter, radiosity glow, a short brown-orange smog, matte vertex-lit materials

noir.desc: black-and-white film noir: crushed blacks, hot highlights, a hard key light with crisp shadows, smoky air, heavy grain

diorama.desc: tilt-shift miniature world: a narrow sharp band across the hero, strong lens blur above and below, toy-bright saturated colours, glossy plastic, the world on twos

cel.desc: cel-shaded graphic novel: the light in two hard steps, flat colour fields, black ink outlines on figures, vehicles and buildings, matte, crisp (no motion blur, no grain)

clay_lite.desc: stop-motion clay set: plasticine on every surface (thumb-pressed lumps, soft wrap light, flat pressed colours), putty faceless puppets, warm studio light, shallow focus, the world on twos

game.desc: QUEST 3D video game: a bright low-poly toy world, chibi figures with faces (big heads, dot eyes, blush), soft sun shadows, clean saturated colour, gentle bloom on gold and chrome, no grain

hologram.desc: holographic projection: the subject as cyan light with glowing edges and rim on a dark void (ground and plants sunk into the dark), scanlines and a slow scan sweep

fern.desc: fern-grade documentary film: low-key 3D lit by one motivated light, fine clumped film grain, slow gate weave, a breath of flicker, red halation round the practicals, specks of dust, a heavy oval vignette; the colour script (blue night, sepia desk, red void) stays per shot

nocturne.desc: fern blue night for the whole film: a deep blue duotone (navy blacks, moon-blue highlights), silhouettes with cool rim light, soft bloom, heavy oval vignette, fine film grain and slow gate weave; red keep_hue lights stay red
